newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire parliament adopts draft new constitution.
newsitem.headline: Zaire parliament adopts draft new constitution.

text.p: Zaire's interim parliament adopted a draft new constitution providing for a federal structure and limiting the president's tenure to two terms, lawmakers said on Sunday.
The draft splits the vast Central African country into 26 provinces, from the 11 in the present unitary system.

The constitution, voted after a session that lasted well into Sunday morning, will be presented for approval in a national referendum before presidential and parliamentary elections due by May next year.
Zaire's transition to democracy has dragged for more than five years and looks threatened again by strongman president Mobutu Sese Seko's prostrate surgery in Europe in August.

Mobutu has wielded absolute power in Zaire for most of the time since seizing power in 1965 and most Zaireans believe a drawn-out period of recuperation from his illness would certainly delay elections in which he has declared his intention to contest.
A senior member of the transition government added weight to fears of such a delay in a news conference in Belgium on Friday.

"The road is still long and dangerous but I am convinced elections will take place next year, perhaps not as scheduled, but by December 31 at the latest," said Christophe Lutundula Apala Pen' Apala, second vice-president of Zaire's High Council of the Republic -- the transitional government.
